language-atlas.method: Canonical IDs are exact Glottocodes; unknown samples and internal study clades retain source-specific IDs. Original sample labels remain on source-tagged edges. Tree hypotheses are never combined across sources as one asserted ancestry. Incompatibility is computed only between rooted summary topologies restricted to at least three shared, non-repeated, non-ancestor tip IDs. Sample absence and polytomies alone are not classified as conflict. Source-specific summary trees, not posterior samples, are imported.

debate.title: Transeurasian relationship
debate.status: Disputed genealogical proposal; no consensus implied
debate.position: Under the Transeurasian hypothesis, Japonic, Koreanic, Tungusic, Mongolic and Turkic are branches of one proposed genealogical group.

This critique argues that the linguistic, genetic and archaeological analyses do not provide conclusive evidence for that family or its proposed farming dispersal. This is rejection of the evidence, not a demonstrated alternative superfamily.
The response revises datasets and approaches while defending the proposed relationship and the triangulation argument.
